description: Article proof dependencies at the level of the formally proved cases actually used. This is not a module-import or task-allocation graph.

nodes.title: Theorem 1.1: compact construction
nodes.scope: The compact candidate, energy bound and early-zero interval at every positive viscosity.

nodes.title: Same-force comparison
nodes.scope: For every positive viscosity, any compact candidate excludes a global smooth same-force solution with uniformly bounded kinetic energy. All reference bounds follow from its proved smoothness, compact support and energy bound.

nodes.title: Theorem 1.1: complete statement
nodes.scope: One time-one compact candidate and its same-force global nonexistence conclusion for every positive viscosity, proved by source_breakdown.

nodes.title: Proposition 2.1: periodic H3 route
nodes.scope: Periodic existence, uniqueness, maximality and continuation for the used force class, using the formally proved H3 restart case.

nodes.title: Proposition 2.1: whole-space H7 route
nodes.scope: Whole-space existence, uniqueness, maximality and continuation for the used force class, using fixed-force H7 restart.

nodes.title: Proposition 2.1: general H1 restart
nodes.scope: The general H1-uniform restart clauses remain unformalized. They are not inputs to the proved H3/H7 continuation routes.

nodes.title: Lemma 2.2: energy and initial vanishing
nodes.scope: Finite energy and dissipation, the energy identity and an initial zero interval for the selected candidate.

nodes.title: Lemma 3.2: fractional localization
nodes.scope: Local-to-torus Sobolev comparison, including the endpoint identities.

nodes.title: Proposition 3.3: scaling
nodes.scope: Energy, mixed-norm and Sobolev scaling of the compact building block.

nodes.title: Lemma 3.4: potential and cutoffs
nodes.scope: Construct a local vector potential and divergence-free cutoff modification.

nodes.title: Lemma 3.5: proved local estimates
nodes.scope: Local support, derivative, energy and mixed-norm bounds with the smoothness and geometric hypotheses supplied by a smooth reference solution.

nodes.title: Lemma 3.5: proved periodic case
nodes.scope: The formal periodic correction theorem with its explicit smoothness, chart and viscosity hypotheses; those hypotheses are supplied in the fixed-ball construction.

nodes.title: Lemma 3.5: full article scope
nodes.scope: Lemma 3.5 for a periodic classical reference on [0,T+δ), positive viscosity, the building-block placement and Lemma 3.4 ball. The zero extension is identified on the slab; all 45 API fields and the displayed derivative, support, energy, mixed and Sobolev bounds are retained, with the force identified globally with the article reference.

nodes.title: Theorem 3.6: fixed-ball construction
nodes.scope: Construct the scaling and correction inputs from raw data; exact lifespan, history and convergence for the fixed-ball case used in density.

nodes.title: Theorem 3.6: prescribed ball
nodes.scope: Theorem 3.6 from raw data for every prescribed positive-radius coordinate ball whose closure lies in the interior of the fundamental cube. The registered packet supplies the building block; only article hypotheses are arguments. Includes exact lifespan, blowup, history, divergence-free single-chart shrinking support, simultaneous energy/mixed/Sobolev bounds and negative-order convergence.

nodes.title: Proposition 3.7: periodic density
nodes.scope: The two-case lifespan argument needs only one fully constructed localization, not the prescribed-ball extension.

nodes.title: Proposition 3.8: periodic critical estimate
nodes.scope: Small critical forcing gives regularity through the proved H3 continuation route.

nodes.title: Corollary 3.9: non-density
nodes.scope: A nonempty open regularity ball and Sobolev monotonicity exclude density at and above the threshold.

nodes.title: Theorem 3.1: periodic threshold
nodes.scope: Combine subcritical fixed-datum density and the zero-datum non-density obstruction.

nodes.title: Corollary 3.10: mixed-norm density
nodes.scope: Use the same two-case argument and the positive mixed-norm scaling exponent.

nodes.title: Corollary 3.11: trajectory closure
nodes.scope: Energy and force convergence for one constructed family around a smooth reference.

nodes.title: Proposition 3.12: data-pair projection
nodes.scope: Fixed-initial-data density gives product density and surjectivity onto the initial-data class.

nodes.title: Remark 3.13: force-amplitude divergence
nodes.scope: For every inserted family, the force-difference supremum is at least epsilon^(-3) times the positive finite packet-force amplitude minus correction.forceProfileConst(0) times epsilon^(-2), and diverges as epsilon decreases to zero. Packet forcing is nonzero by energy and blowup; includes the constructed T19 fixed-ball family. Extended amplitudes tend to nhds top and finite real amplitudes to atTop.

nodes.title: Bounded-domain norm comparison
nodes.scope: Restriction and zero-extension estimates for compactly supported interior perturbations.

nodes.title: No-slip uniqueness
nodes.scope: The classical uniqueness theorem on the bounded domain is formally proved.

nodes.title: Corollary 3.14: bounded-domain gluing
nodes.scope: The final raw-data theorem constructs its packet, placement and norm witnesses internally in the prescribed interior ball.

nodes.title: Proposition 3.15: affine variations
nodes.scope: Compact divergence-free perturbations of the selected building block give the affine family.

nodes.title: Proposition 3.16: periodic regions
nodes.scope: Place finitely many rescaled building blocks in prescribed disjoint periodic regions and sum them.

nodes.title: Proposition 3.16: bounded-domain case
nodes.scope: The bounded-domain no-slip variant has not been assembled.

nodes.title: Proposition 3.17: periodic conservative force
nodes.scope: Potential-force pairing vanishes and the solution from rest has zero velocity on the torus.

nodes.title: Proposition 3.17: bounded-domain case
nodes.scope: For every smooth spacetime potential on a bounded box-or-regular-level domain with homogeneous no-slip, the force-velocity pairing vanishes; at positive viscosity every classical solution from rest has zero velocity throughout its lifespan.

nodes.title: Whole-space negative-order estimates
nodes.scope: Fourier scaling and low-frequency control of compact force profiles; the positive and negative norm bounds needed for the subcritical limits.

nodes.title: Theorem 4.2: prescribed-region gluing
nodes.scope: For every prescribed nonempty open set, construct one family from the given reference, with exact lifespan, blowup, history, compact support, energy bound and all subcritical force limits. The building block is selected before the reference and region.

nodes.title: Proposition 4.3: L1 critical estimate
nodes.scope: The whole-space critical estimate with the proved high-order continuation route.

nodes.title: Proposition 4.4: L2 critical estimate
nodes.scope: The finite-horizon inhomogeneous critical estimate at zero initial velocity.

nodes.title: Theorem 4.1: whole-space thresholds
nodes.scope: Combine subcritical density from the constructed case with the two critical non-density obstructions.

nodes.title: Corollary 4.5: compact and rapid-decay classes
nodes.scope: Compactly supported force changes preserve both subclasses; the same critical regularity balls give the converse.

nodes.title: Smooth Sobolev and Bochner approximation
nodes.scope: Approximate completed data by smooth compactly supported fields and time profiles.

nodes.title: Proposition 4.6: completed spaces and trajectories
nodes.scope: Combine smooth approximation, compact-force density and the simultaneous energy and force estimates for one family.

nodes.title: Grid-adapted local construction
nodes.scope: Construct a ball inside a common cell and prove vanishing cell integrals for the localized perturbation.

nodes.title: Theorem 4.7: identical grid observations
nodes.scope: Use the internally constructed common-cell ball, cancellation and simultaneous convergence estimates.
